what: Kernel profile at production shape with fused norm + FlexAttention + fused CE all on
run: .runs/prodce/profile (16x L40S, seq8192, tp1 dp16, GA8, bf16 grad reduce)

history_percent.note: Same model and shape; each column is a later optimization state.

categorization_correction: FlexAttention compiles to Inductor template kernels (triton_tem_fused_*). They were first counted as 'other', which reported attention at 0.62%. They are the attention: with PRETRAIN_FLEX_ATTENTION=0 they are absent and fmha_cutlass* appear at the same share. The parser now classifies them.

findings.finding: GEMM is now the single largest category at 41.8%
findings.implication: Arithmetic, not framework overhead, now dominates. This is what FP8 would attack; see fp8_ceiling.json for the measured bound.
Multi-node data-parallel communication is not a bottleneck at GA=8 with BF16 gradient reduction. Per-card throughput rose from 2 to 16 cards.

findings.finding: Two more CUDA reference fallbacks were still live: the backbone SwiGLU and the GDN causal convolution, both dispatching on device.type == 'npu'
findings.implication: The SwiGLU ran as chunk+silu+mul and the convolution ran a Python loop of F.conv1d per packed document. Both have published kernels in the same upstream library already supplying the GDN recurrence.

findings.finding: copy/index reached 12% -- index_select/index_add/cat over the CQ event plan
findings.implication: This is the architecture's own layout machinery, not a port artifact. Reducing it would mean restructuring the GDN event gather, which is on the protected CPU-plan boundary.

method: torch.profiler chrome trace, kernels attributed to their launching aten op through correlation ids. Shares are of total GPU kernel time, not wall time; kernels overlap, so these do not sum to step time.
